A particle moves along the curve defined by the equation $y=x^{3}-3 x$. The $x$-coordinate of the particle, $x(t)$, satisfies the equation $\frac{d x}{d t}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2 t+1}}$, for $t \geq 0$ with initial condition $x(0)=-4$.\\
(a) Find $x(t)$ in terms of $t$.\\
(b) Find $\frac{d y}{d t}$ in terms of $t$.\\
(c) Find the location and speed of the particle at time $t=4$.

\begin{itemize}\item[6.] A particle moves along the curve defined by the equation \(y=x^{3}-3 x\). The \(x\)-coordinate of the particle, \(x(t)\), satisfies the equation \(\frac{d x}{d t}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2 t+1}}\), for \(t \geq 0\) with initial condition \(x(0)=-4\).
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] Find \(x(t)\) in terms of \(t\).
\item[(b)] Find \(\frac{d y}{d t}\) in terms of \(t\).
\item[(c)] Find the location and speed of the particle at time \(t=4\).
\end{itemize}
\item[(a)] \(x(t)=\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{2 t+1}} d t\)
\[
\begin{aligned}
& x(t)=\sqrt{2 t+1}+C \\
& x(0)=-4=1+C \Rightarrow C=-5 \\
& x(t)=\sqrt{2 t+1}-5
\end{aligned}
\]
\item[(b)] \(y=x^{3}-3 x\)
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{d y}{d t} & =3 x^{2} \frac{d x}{d t}-3 \frac{d x}{d t} \\
& =\left(3 x^{2}-3\right) \frac{d x}{d t} \\
& =\left[3(\sqrt{2 t+1}-5)^{2}-3\right]\left[\frac{1}{\sqrt{2 t+1}}\right]
\end{aligned}
\]
\item[(c)] \(x(4)=\sqrt{9}-5=-2\)
\[
y(4)=(-2)^{3}-3(-2)=-2
\]
Location at \(t=4\) is ( \(-2,-2\) )
\[
\begin{aligned}
& \left.\frac{d x}{d t}\right|_{t=4}=\frac{1}{3} \\
& \left.\frac{d y}{d t}\right|_{t=4}=\frac{3(3-5)^{2}-3}{3}=3 \\
& \text { Speed }=\sqrt{\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{2}+3^{2}}=\sqrt{\frac{82}{9}}=3.018
\end{aligned}
\]
\end{itemize}
